enacting_law: Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Pub. L. 93-112, § 504, 87 Stat. 394 (September 26, 1973)
effective_date: 1973-09-26 (statute); 1977-04-28 (implementing regulations — delayed by HEW for four years)
verified_note: USC tool blocked for Title 29 at build time; text from training knowledge. Verify at uscode.house.gov.
wound_record: Pre-1973: no federal law prohibited exclusion of disabled individuals from federally-funded programs. § 504 was modeled on Title VI (race discrimination) and Title IX (sex discrimination) — brief add-on with sweeping implications that its drafters may not have fully recognized. HEW then refused to issue implementing regulations for four years, rendering the statute unenforceable. The 1977 sit-in (25 days in San Francisco HEW office; solidarity from Black Panther Party, UFW) forced Secretary Califano to sign the regulations. Grove City College v. Bell (1984) then narrowed the statute to program-specific coverage, forcing Congress to pass the CRRA (1987) to restore institution-wide coverage.
crra_note: Civil Rights Restoration Act of 1987 (Pub. L. 100-259) — enacted over President Reagan's veto; restored institution-wide coverage; if any part of an entity receives federal funds, all programs of that entity are covered by §504, Title VI, Title IX, and Age Discrimination Act
key_milestones: 1973-09-26: §504 enacted (three sentences; sweeping implication not initially recognized)
1973–1977: HEW refuses to issue implementing regulations
1977-04-05: Disability rights organizations occupy HEW offices in 8 cities
1977-04-28: HEW Secretary Califano signs Section 504 regulations (San Francisco occupation: 25 days)
1984: Grove City College v. Bell narrows §504 to program-specific coverage
1987-03-22: CRRA enacted — institution-wide coverage restored; Grove City reversed
